title: Critical Language Awareness
summary: How language persuades and manipulates: fact and opinion, bias, stereotyping, emotive language, denotation and connotation, and persuasive techniques in the media.

items: **Fact**: can be proved: 'Cape Town is in the Western Cape.'
**Opinion**: a belief or judgement: 'Cape Town is the most beautiful city.'
**Bias**: a one-sided view that favours or opposes something unfairly.
**Stereotype**: an oversimplified belief about a whole group ('All teenagers are lazy').

notes.text: **Emotive language** stirs feelings: 'innocent children' or 'a shocking disaster'. Word choice shows the writer's attitude: protesters can be called 'activists' (positive) or 'a mob' (negative). This is the difference between **denotation** (literal meaning) and **connotation** (associations).

rows: 'Don't you want your family to be safe?'

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: When asked how language manipulates, name the technique, quote it, and explain its effect on the reader.

options: The FIFA World Cup was held in South Africa in 2010.

questions.prompt: What is an oversimplified belief about a whole group of people called?
'Join the millions who have switched!' uses which technique?
Using 'we' and 'us' in a speech makes the audience feel included.
'This is the tastiest pizza in Durban' is a fact.
Match each example to its technique.
A newspaper calls a group of strikers 'a mob'. Explain the effect of this word.
questions.memo:
✓ 'Mob' has negative connotations of violence/disorder (1)
✓ It makes readers see the strikers unfavourably, showing bias (1)

questions.prompt: Rewrite neutrally: 'The greedy taxi bosses have once again hiked fares.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'Taxi associations have increased fares again.' (emotive words removed) (2)

questions.prompt: Explain why 'Girls are bad at maths' is a stereotype and why it is harmful.
questions.memo:
✓ It generalises about all girls without evidence (1)
✓ It can discourage girls and limit their opportunities (1)

questions.prompt: Why might a reader be sceptical of 'Nine out of ten dentists recommend Brite toothpaste'?
questions.memo:
✓ We are not told how many dentists were asked or who paid for the survey (1)
✓ The claim is designed to persuade, not inform (1)
